gap: No result ChatGPT got works out what it costs to run the box 24/7. At the August 2026 US residential average of 18.16¢/kWh, the Synology DS225+ costs about $27 a year at its rated 16.98 W 'Access' draw ($9.67 a year with the drives hibernating). The UGREEN DXP2800 family costs $11–$32 a year, depending on the idle draw a named reviewer measured. Over five years that is $50–$160, well below the gap in purchase price and RAM between the two.
standout_why: I compared against racksandwatts.com/guides/best-nas-for-a-homelab-2026 (cited). It gives RAM and bay counts only, with no wattage, running cost or prices; I opened it. The cited Synology DS425+ HIG, the UGREEN buying guides and mariushosting are spec or setup pages with no running-cost arithmetic. I couldn't open ai.ugreen.com because it returned HTTP 429. None of ChatGPT's three answers mentions power or electricity cost, even though an always-on family server runs 8,760 hours a year. The figure is new and useful, but it is small, so it doesn't decide the pick on its own.
decides: It confirms the pick and doesn't change it. Running costs for the DS225+ and DXP2800 are within about $5–$15 a year of each other, so electricity can't make up for the DS225+'s 2 GB RAM (6 GB maximum, and non-Synology RAM voids its warranty). The DXP2800 comes with 8 GB and costs $389.99 at UGREEN's own store today. That price is not the $296.99 Walmart price ChatGPT showed. The page should present running cost as 'about $1–$3 a month either way' and let RAM, price and software decide.
